title: Physics: notable papers from the arXiv 2026-10-23 announcement batch
global_caveat: arXiv supplies no official trending chart; the ordering is inferred from checkable signals, and citation evidence is sparse for papers announced only hours or days ago. It is not a measured popularity ranking.

sections.title: Lifetime of the singly charged $^{229}$Th nuclear isomer
sections.abstract: The authors use an ion trap and internal-conversion electron detection to measure a 0.46(8)-s half-life for singly charged $^{229m}$Th, which they interpret as indirect evidence for electronic-bridge decay.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report a 0.46(8)-s half-life for $^{229m}$Th$^+$, several orders of magnitude different from the known internal-conversion and radiative-decay lifetimes, and infer that electronic-bridge decay is a likely channel.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; charge-exchange production in an ion trap and microchannel-plate detection of internal-conversion electrons, with pressure-dependent measurements.
sections.unique_caveat: Electronic-bridge decay is inferred rather than directly observed; the authors identify a 0.17 s^-1 systematic uncertainty in the fitted decay constant and call for direct photon detection.

sections.title: Realization of a Superleak in a Quantum Gas
sections.abstract: An optical superlattice separates fast coherent superfluid transport from slow normal-fluid transport, enabling repeated filtering and sustained driven oscillations in an ultracold gas.
sections.claimed_result: In 87Rb gases, the authors report a dynamical superleak with a measured 500(49) flow-rate contrast, increasing the condensate fraction from about 50% to 94(1)% after four filtering cycles.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; ultracold 87Rb in an optical superlattice, with site-resolved band-mapping and time-of-flight imaging, supported by microscopic modeling.
sections.unique_caveat: Filtering is imperfect: the authors report retaining 57% of the initial superfluid after four cycles and attribute some loss to limited site selectivity; the demonstration uses a specific quasi-2D lattice setup.

sections.title: Odd radio circle J1555+2726: Observational evidence for shock re-acceleration of fossil plasma
sections.abstract: Multi-frequency radio maps of ORC4 show spectral and morphological features that the authors interpret as a shock re-accelerating a pre-existing population of relativistic electrons.
sections.claimed_result: From an integrated spectral slope of 1.06±0.03, radial spectral flattening, and negative spectral curvature, the authors argue that standard shock acceleration of thermal particles plus ordinary ageing is insufficient and favor re-acceleration of fossil plasma.
sections.evidence_type: Observational; LOFAR, upgraded GMRT, and MeerKAT radio observations over 50–1284 MHz, supplemented by survey images and spectral-index analysis.
sections.unique_caveat: The proposed 3-D geometry is phenomenological; available X-ray data are too shallow to constrain the shock Mach number independently, and the paper discusses flux-scale and resolution effects.

ranking_signals.comment: Resubmitted to A&A after referee report

sections.title: First Results of Calculation of the Dayside Magnetopause Reconnection Rate with TRACERS
sections.abstract: The authors apply an ion-dispersion method to early TRACERS spacecraft observations to estimate dayside reconnection rates during two geomagnetic storms.
sections.claimed_result: For one storm, 21 ion-dispersion events yield estimated reconnection rates generally between 0.1 and 1.5 mV/m; onset/main-phase rates correlate with SuperDARN cross-polar-cap potential (r^2=0.62), while the relationship disappears when recovery-phase events are included.
sections.evidence_type: Observational; TRACERS-2 ion measurements compared with SuperDARN-derived cross-polar-cap potential and an automatic ion-dispersion identification algorithm.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported correlation is phase-dependent and based on a small number of storm events; the authors frame the algorithm as groundwork for future statistical analysis.
sections.journal_status: Under revision for Journal of Geophysical Research: Space Physics

sections.title: Experimental evidence of forward energy transfer induced by core-edge coupling in multiscale tokamak turbulence
sections.abstract: The authors combine core and edge turbulence diagnostics in a tokamak and report evidence consistent with an edge-originating quasi-coherent mode coupling to core turbulence and transferring energy toward smaller scales.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report measurements consistent with a net forward transfer from ion to electron scales associated with a quasi-coherent edge mode resonantly coupled to broadband core turbulence.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; combined collective Thomson scattering and Doppler backscattering measurements of tokamak fluctuations.
sections.unique_caveat: The result is evidence consistent with the proposed transfer mechanism, tied to the measured tokamak regime and interpretation of the observed mode coupling.

sections.title: Observation of Polarization Topology in Magneto-Optical BICs
sections.abstract: The authors reconstruct the momentum-space polarization texture of a magneto-optical bound state in the continuum and report a topological charge of +1 and magnetically reversible polarization handedness.
sections.claimed_result: The authors extract a counterclockwise 2π polarization winding and charge q=+1 around the Γ-point singularity, while reversing polarization handedness by changing magnetic bias without changing the charge.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; polarization-resolved angle-resolved reflection-matrix measurements analyzed by singular-value decomposition, interpreted with a non-Hermitian coupled-mode model.
sections.unique_caveat: The result concerns the measured magneto-optical BIC and its modeled mode hybridization; broad generalization to other structures is not established in the abstract.

sections.title: In situ performance of the Vertex Silicon Plane in the BM@N experiment during Run 9
sections.abstract: The authors report commissioning and in-situ tracking performance for a six-module silicon plane installed in the BM@N experiment during Run 9.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report signal-to-noise ratios of 15.5–33.2, about 12 ns timing resolution, and approximately 95% hit-matching efficiency, with the plane extending near-target tracking acceptance.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; in-situ BM@N Run 9 detector data, with Forward Silicon Detector and Gas Electron Multiplier tracking references.
sections.unique_caveat: These are commissioning and Run 9 performance results for one detector installation; performance across later operating conditions or runs is not established here.

sections.title: Cleaner air strengthens the Pacific trade winds without a detectable change in El Nino
sections.abstract: An ensemble of 12 Earth-system models suggests that air-quality emission cuts strengthen future Pacific trade winds, while the ensemble cannot detect a substantial change in ENSO amplitude.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find in their model ensemble that air-quality controls offset roughly half to two-thirds of projected Pacific trade-wind weakening, with the response emerging after 2040; ENSO-amplitude changes remain below one tenth of baseline amplitude and below the ensemble's detection threshold.
sections.evidence_type: Computational; 12 Earth-system-model experiments with and without air-quality controls, plus prescribed-SST and regional-emission comparisons.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a model-based future response, not an observed climate change; the wind result depends on the coupled response and appears only after 2040, while the ensemble cannot resolve a meaningful ENSO-amplitude shift.

sections.title: Entanglement certification of attosecond light fields with photoelectron interferometry
sections.abstract: The paper develops separability and multipartite-entanglement witnesses for attosecond XUV light, showing how photoelectron interferometry could access the required optical correlation functions.
sections.claimed_result: The author derives a negative-partial-transpose witness for infrared–XUV entanglement and a sufficient witness for genuine multipartite entanglement without auxiliary optical measurements, then evaluates them on explicit optical states.
sections.evidence_type: Theoretical; quantum-optical treatment mapping photoelectron interferometry to optical correlation functions and evaluation on explicit states.
sections.unique_caveat: The witnesses are proposed and evaluated theoretically; no experimental certification or quantified robustness to experimental noise is reported in the abstract.
